description: We are a dedicated team from Sri Lanka passionate about turning complex NASA space data into engaging, easy-to-understand stories and visuals. By combining research, creative storytelling, UI/UX design, and AI tools, we aim to inspire people and solve real-world challenge
summary: Abandoned, But Not Forgotten: Interactive Space Museum is an educational, single-page web application designed to bring the untold stories of NASA's discarded lunar and Martian hardware to life for both school-age students and adults. Using custom SVG graphics, smooth planetary travel animations, an interactive 57-year mission timeline, and a gamified Space Detective Quiz, our platform transforms static space archives into an engaging digital adventure. Users can explore five iconic artifacts—including the Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Mars Opportunity Rover, Curiosity's Sky Crane, and the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter—uncovering their secret stories, real scientific breakthroughs, and current statuses on the Moon and Mars.
details: What It Does & How It Works: Our interactive digital museum allows users to seamlessly travel between the Moon and Mars via animated rocket and rover transitions. Visitors can click on glowing timeline nodes or interactive hardware cards to open detailed story modals featuring The Secret Story, Real Science Made Possible, Current Status, and Fun Facts. It also includes a 5-question Space Detective Quiz with instant score tracking and celebratory confetti animations. Tools & Technologies Used: Built as a lightweight, zero-dependency, self-contained single-page application using HTML5, CSS3 animations, Vanilla JavaScript, and custom inline SVG artwork, hosted live via GitHub Pages. Creative Impact: By combining storytelling with interactive gamification, we bridge the gap between complex NASA archival data and young learners worldwide.
